items.text: The child's idea works! The builder looks surprised, then proud.
The child's idea fails harmlessly. The builder helps (child.him/her) understand why, and they try a better method together.
The child hammers the wrong piece. The elder laughs so hard that (elder.he/she) nearly falls off the old bench.
The child gets frustrated and declares that building is stupid. The builder admits that (builder.he/she) has felt that way too.
The child carefully measures the wood and discovers the builder was about to cut the wrong length. The builder goes very quiet.
The builder repairs the bench neatly, then lets the child practice on spare wood. The child beams.
The builder works too quickly to explain. The child wanders away, disappointed. The elder gently points this out.
The builder tries to demonstrate a perfect joint and accidentally glues (builder.his/her) own fingers together.
The builder finishes, then admits that the child's question exposed a flaw in the original design.
"You can teach a child to hold a tool," the elder says. "The harder part is teaching (child.him/her) not to fear mistakes."
"When I was young, my teacher shouted whenever I got something wrong. I remember the shouting better than the lessons."
"I once built a whole hut backward," the elder confesses. "Nobody noticed until we tried to put the door in."
"That bench will outlast the argument," the elder says. The builder hopes this is true.
The child proudly sits on the finished bench. It holds. For the moment, that is enough.
The builder asks the child to help again tomorrow. The child replies, "Only if you answer my questions."
The elder leaves a tiny carved wooden bird on the bench. Nobody knows when (elder.he/she) made it.
The bench collapses under a basket of coconuts. Nobody is injured. The builder stares at the wreckage and sighs, "Well. That's a useful test."
The child falls asleep on the newly repaired bench. The builder quietly gathers the tools and lets (child.him/her) rest.

intro.name: The bench
intro.text:
A respected Master Builder, (Builder), has been asked to repair a small wooden bench outside the school. The job is simple enough that (builder.he/she) expects to finish before lunch.
Unfortunately, (Child) has decided to help.
"Why are you doing it like that?" asks (Child). "Because it works." "But why?" "Because - " The builder pauses. "Because it works."
An elderly villager, (Elder), watches from a nearby seat, looking far too entertained.

question.name: The child's idea
question.text: The child notices that the bench has {a wobbling leg|a loose joint|a splintered edge|a crooked support} and proposes {a ridiculous solution|a clever fix|a solution copied from something (child.he/she) saw the builder do earlier}.

choices.label: LET THE CHILD TRY WITH SUPERVISION.
FINISH THE REPAIR, THEN EXPLAIN IT.
